name: Abdomen
definition: The region of the body between the lower ribs and the upper thighs, containing abdominal organs and major blood vessels.
clinical_significance: The abdomen is an important anatomical region for describing the location of abdominal aortic disease, vascular injury, internal bleeding, and symptoms that may arise from abdominal organs.

name: Abdominal aorta
definition: The segment of the aorta that runs through the abdomen after the vessel passes below the diaphragm and before it divides into the iliac arteries.
clinical_significance: Disease of the abdominal aorta can alter blood flow to abdominal organs and the lower limbs; aneurysm, dissection, or occlusion in this segment can therefore be clinically serious.

name: Ablation
definition: A procedure that destroys or removes a selected area of tissue. In cardiac ablation, the targeted tissue may be treated with heat, freezing, or another energy source.
clinical_significance: Cardiac ablation can eliminate or isolate tissue that initiates or maintains an abnormal heart rhythm, making it an important treatment approach for selected arrhythmias.

name: ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor
definition: A medicine that inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, reducing the formation of angiotensin II, a substance that constricts blood vessels and promotes sodium and water retention.
clinical_significance: By reducing angiotensin II activity, an ACE inhibitor lowers vascular resistance and blood pressure and reduces the workload imposed on the heart.

name: Acetylcholine
definition: A neurotransmitter released by nerve cells that carries signals to other nerve cells and to muscle cells by binding to specific receptors.
clinical_significance: Acetylcholine mediates parasympathetic effects on the heart, including slowing activity at the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes, and is therefore relevant to cardiac rate and conduction.

name: Acquired heart disease
definition: A disorder of the heart or cardiovascular system that develops after birth rather than being present as a congenital defect. Causes include infection and atherosclerotic plaque in the coronary arteries.
clinical_significance: The term distinguishes disease acquired during life from congenital heart disease; depending on its cause, it may impair myocardial blood supply, valve function, rhythm, or the heart's pumping ability.

name: Alveoli
definition: Microscopic air sacs at the ends of the smallest airways in the lungs, surrounded by capillaries and specialized for the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide.
clinical_significance: Alveolar gas exchange oxygenates blood and removes carbon dioxide; damage or fluid within the alveoli can impair oxygenation and place additional stress on the cardiovascular system.

name: Amiodarone
definition: A class III antiarrhythmic medicine that alters cardiac electrical activity and is used to treat rhythm disturbances such as atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia.
clinical_significance: Amiodarone can suppress clinically important atrial and ventricular arrhythmias and is often reserved for patients whose rhythm disturbance has not responded adequately to other antiarrhythmic medicines.

name: Aneurysm
definition: A localized abnormal widening or bulging of a blood vessel or a heart wall caused by weakening of the vessel wall or cardiac muscle.
clinical_significance: An aneurysm represents structural weakness that can enlarge over time and, depending on its location and severity, may dissect, rupture, impair blood flow, or generate emboli.

name: Angina or angina pectoris
definition: A symptom of myocardial ischemia, usually experienced as pressure, tightness, or discomfort in the chest when the coronary circulation cannot supply enough oxygen to the heart muscle.
clinical_significance: Angina commonly reflects underlying coronary artery disease and indicates an imbalance between myocardial oxygen supply and demand; a new, worsening, or rest pattern may signify more severe ischemia.

name: Angiography
definition: An imaging procedure in which a radiopaque contrast agent is introduced into the heart or blood vessels and x-ray images are obtained to show the vessel lumen and the passage of blood.
clinical_significance: Cardiac and coronary angiography can identify arterial narrowing or occlusion and characterize cardiac or vascular anatomy, helping clinicians evaluate ischemic disease and plan catheter-based treatment.

name: Angioplasty
definition: A catheter-based procedure in which a balloon is inflated within a narrowed artery to compress plaque and enlarge the arterial lumen; a stent may also be placed to help keep the vessel open.
clinical_significance: Angioplasty restores or improves blood flow through a stenotic artery and is used as a revascularization procedure, including in selected coronary and peripheral arterial disease.

name: Angiotensin II receptor blocker
definition: A medicine that blocks the effects of angiotensin II at its receptors, reducing vasoconstriction and the associated retention of sodium and water.
clinical_significance: By opposing angiotensin II signaling, an angiotensin II receptor blocker lowers vascular resistance and blood pressure and reduces the afterload against which the heart pumps.

name: Annulus
definition: The fibrous ring surrounding a heart-valve opening, to which the valve leaflets or cusps are attached and which helps maintain the shape of the orifice.
clinical_significance: The size and shape of a valve annulus affect leaflet coaptation and valve competence; annular enlargement can contribute to regurgitation and is important in echocardiographic and procedural valve assessment.

name: Antiarrhythmics
definition: A group of medicines that modify cardiac electrical activity, including impulse formation, conduction, or refractoriness, to treat abnormal heart rhythms.
clinical_significance: Antiarrhythmics are used to suppress or prevent clinically significant atrial or ventricular arrhythmias and may help restore or maintain an effective cardiac rhythm.

name: Anticoagulant
definition: A medicine that inhibits one or more steps in the blood-coagulation cascade, reducing the formation or growth of fibrin-containing blood clots.
clinical_significance: Anticoagulants reduce the risk of thrombosis and embolism in appropriate cardiovascular conditions, but their effect also increases the potential for clinically important bleeding.

name: Antihypertensive
definition: A medicine or therapeutic intervention used to reduce persistently elevated arterial blood pressure by lowering vascular resistance, reducing cardiac output, decreasing circulating volume, or using another blood-pressure-lowering mechanism.
clinical_significance: Antihypertensive treatment reduces the hemodynamic burden on the heart and arteries and is used to lower the risk of complications associated with sustained hypertension, including cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease.

name: Antiplatelet therapy
definition: Treatment with medicines that inhibit platelet activation and aggregation, thereby reducing formation of the platelet-rich component of a blood clot.
clinical_significance: Antiplatelet therapy is particularly relevant to arterial thrombosis, where platelet aggregation contributes to vessel occlusion; its principal treatment-related hazard is increased bleeding.

name: Aorta
definition: The body's largest artery, arising from the left ventricle and carrying oxygenated blood through the ascending aorta, arch, and descending thoracic and abdominal segments to the systemic circulation.
clinical_significance: The aorta is the principal conduit for systemic blood flow; diseases such as aneurysm, dissection, or obstruction can compromise perfusion of major organs and may be life-threatening.

name: Aortic valve
definition: The usually three-cusped valve between the left ventricle and the aorta that opens during ventricular contraction to permit forward flow and closes during relaxation to prevent backflow.
clinical_significance: Aortic stenosis obstructs left-ventricular ejection, whereas aortic regurgitation allows blood to return to the ventricle; either lesion can increase cardiac workload and impair effective systemic output.

name: Aphasia
definition: An acquired disorder of language caused by injury or disease affecting the brain's language networks, impairing the production or comprehension of speech and sometimes reading or writing.
clinical_significance: Aphasia is an important neurological sign of dominant-hemisphere dysfunction, commonly after stroke, and helps indicate the location and functional impact of cerebral injury.

name: Arrhythmia (or dysrhythmia)
definition: An abnormality of the heart's rate, rhythm, or electrical impulse formation or conduction, producing a heartbeat that may be too fast, too slow, irregular, or arising from an abnormal site.
clinical_significance: Arrhythmias can reduce cardiac output, cause palpitations, dizziness, or syncope, and in some forms increase the risk of thromboembolism, heart failure, or sudden cardiac death.

name: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia (ARVD)
definition: An inherited cardiomyopathy, also called arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, in which myocardial tissue—predominantly in the right ventricle—is progressively replaced by fibrous or fatty tissue.
clinical_significance: The structural myocardial changes create a substrate for ventricular tachyarrhythmias and may impair right-ventricular function, making ARVD an important cause of syncope, ventricular arrhythmia, and sudden cardiac death in affected families.

name: Arteriography
definition: A contrast-enhanced imaging study of an artery or arterial system, usually performed by injecting radiopaque contrast during catheterization and obtaining images of the arterial lumen.
clinical_significance: Arteriography can demonstrate stenosis, occlusion, aneurysm, or other arterial abnormalities and can provide anatomical guidance for endovascular or surgical planning.

name: Arterioles
definition: Small branches of arteries that lead into capillary beds and contain a prominent layer of smooth muscle capable of changing their diameter.
clinical_significance: Arterioles are the major resistance vessels of the circulation; their constriction or dilation regulates systemic vascular resistance, arterial pressure, and distribution of blood flow to tissues.

name: Artery
definition: A blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart. Most arteries carry oxygenated blood to the tissues, although the pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
clinical_significance: Arterial narrowing, blockage, inflammation, or rupture can reduce or interrupt tissue perfusion, producing ischemia or hemorrhage in the organs supplied by the affected artery.

name: Arteritis
definition: Inflammation of the wall of one or more arteries, caused by an immune-mediated disease, infection, or another inflammatory process.
clinical_significance: Arterial inflammation can thicken or weaken the vessel wall, producing stenosis, thrombosis, aneurysm, or dissection and reducing blood flow to the tissues supplied by the affected arteries.

name: Arteriosclerosis
definition: A general term for thickening, hardening, and loss of elasticity of arterial walls. It includes several processes, including atherosclerosis, arteriolosclerosis, and medial arterial calcification.
clinical_significance: Reduced arterial compliance can increase vascular resistance and pulse pressure, while associated narrowing or plaque formation can limit tissue perfusion and contribute to cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease.

name: Artificial heart
definition: A mechanical prosthesis designed to replace the pumping function of the native heart; a total artificial heart replaces the ventricles and associated valves.
clinical_significance: An artificial heart can provide mechanical circulation for selected patients with severe, otherwise refractory heart failure, often as support while a donor heart is sought; device-related infection, bleeding, or thrombosis are important clinical concerns.

name: Ascending aorta
definition: The proximal segment of the aorta that begins at the aortic valve and extends superiorly to the origin of the aortic arch; its root contains the openings of the coronary arteries.
clinical_significance: Aneurysm, dissection, or other disease of the ascending aorta can compromise the coronary arteries or aortic valve and may threaten the integrity of the aorta itself.

name: Aspirin
definition: Acetylsalicylic acid, a salicylate medicine that provides analgesic, antipyretic, and anti-inflammatory effects and irreversibly inhibits platelet cyclooxygenase at low doses.
clinical_significance: By reducing thromboxane-dependent platelet aggregation, aspirin can lower arterial thrombotic risk in selected cardiovascular settings; its antiplatelet effect also increases the risk of gastrointestinal and other bleeding.

name: Atherectomy
definition: A catheter-based endovascular procedure that removes or modifies atherosclerotic plaque within an artery using a specialized device, such as a cutting, rotating, orbital, or laser system.
clinical_significance: Atherectomy can debulk selected obstructive or heavily calcified lesions to enlarge the arterial lumen and facilitate blood flow or subsequent intervention; procedural complications can include distal embolization or vessel injury.

name: Atherosclerosis
definition: A chronic inflammatory disease of medium and large arteries in which lipid, fibrous tissue, inflammatory cells, and calcium accumulate within the arterial wall to form atherosclerotic plaque.
clinical_significance: Plaque can progressively narrow an artery or rupture and trigger thrombosis, making atherosclerosis a major cause of coronary artery disease, ischemic stroke, and peripheral arterial ischemia.

name: Atrium (right and left)
definition: The two upper chambers of the heart. The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the systemic veins, while the left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins; each passes blood to its corresponding ventricle through an atrioventricular valve.
clinical_significance: The atria serve as reservoirs and contribute to ventricular filling; atrial enlargement, abnormal pressure, or loss of coordinated atrial contraction can impair filling and promote atrial arrhythmias or thrombus formation.

name: Atrial flutter
definition: A supraventricular tachyarrhythmia caused by a rapid, usually organized re-entrant electrical circuit in the atria, producing rapid atrial depolarizations and variable conduction of impulses to the ventricles.
clinical_significance: Atrial flutter can cause palpitations, reduced ventricular filling, or a rapid ventricular response, and the abnormal atrial rhythm can promote atrial thrombus formation and systemic thromboembolism.

name: Atrial septal defect
definition: A congenital opening in the septum between the right and left atria that permits blood to pass between the heart's upper chambers; the direction and size of the shunt depend on relative atrial pressures.
clinical_significance: A significant left-to-right atrial shunt can enlarge and overload the right atrium and ventricle and increase pulmonary blood flow; atrial arrhythmias, pulmonary hypertension, or paradoxical embolism may occur in established disease.

name: Atrial tachycardia
definition: A supraventricular tachyarrhythmia in which rapid electrical impulses arise from an atrial focus rather than the sinoatrial node, producing a rapid atrial and usually ventricular rhythm.
clinical_significance: Atrial tachycardia can cause palpitations, dizziness, or reduced cardiac output; when sustained or recurrent, the rapid rate may impair ventricular function and produce tachycardia-mediated cardiomyopathy.

name: Atrioventricular block
definition: Delayed or failed conduction of electrical impulses from the atria to the ventricles through the atrioventricular node or His–Purkinje conduction system. It may be first-degree, second-degree, or complete (third-degree) block.
clinical_significance: Atrioventricular block can produce bradycardia, loss of coordinated atrial and ventricular contraction, reduced cardiac output, dizziness, or syncope; complete block may cause severe hemodynamic compromise.

name: Atrioventricular (AV) node
definition: A specialized group of conducting cells in the lower interatrial septum that receives impulses from the atria, briefly delays them, and conducts them to the ventricles through the bundle of His.
clinical_significance: The AV node coordinates atrial and ventricular activation and limits transmission of excessively rapid atrial impulses; disease or excessive delay at this site can cause atrioventricular block and bradycardia.

name: Atrium
definition: Either of the heart's two upper chambers. An atrium receives blood returning to the heart and transfers it through an atrioventricular valve into the corresponding ventricle.
clinical_significance: Atrial size, pressure, and rhythm influence ventricular filling; atrial dilation or dysfunction can accompany valve disease, heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, or atrial arrhythmias.

name: Autologous
definition: Derived from the same individual who receives it; an autologous graft, transplant, blood product, or cell preparation is collected from and returned to that person.
clinical_significance: Autologous material generally avoids donor-recipient immunologic incompatibility and is therefore relevant when describing a patient's own vascular graft, stem cells, or other transplanted tissue.

name: Autoregulation
definition: The intrinsic ability of an organ or vascular bed to maintain relatively stable blood flow despite changes in perfusion pressure, mainly through local changes in arteriolar resistance.
clinical_significance: Autoregulation helps preserve tissue perfusion across a range of arterial pressures; failure of this mechanism can make organs, particularly the brain, heart, and kidneys, vulnerable to ischemia or pressure-related injury.

name: Bacteria
definition: Single-celled prokaryotic microorganisms. Many are harmless or beneficial members of the normal microbiota, while pathogenic species can invade tissues and cause infection.
clinical_significance: Bacteria can enter the bloodstream and cause bacteremia, sepsis, or infection of abnormal heart valves and the endocardium; identifying the organism is important for classifying and managing cardiovascular infection.

name: Bacterial endocarditis
definition: An infection of the endocardial surface of the heart, most often involving one or more heart valves, caused by bacteria circulating in the bloodstream and forming infected vegetations.
clinical_significance: Bacterial endocarditis can destroy valve tissue, cause severe regurgitation and heart failure, and release infected emboli; it is therefore a potentially life-threatening cardiovascular infection.

name: Balloon catheter
definition: A thin, flexible catheter with an inflatable balloon near its tip that can be advanced through a blood vessel to a selected site and inflated for a therapeutic or procedural purpose.
clinical_significance: Balloon catheters are used to dilate narrowed arteries or stenotic valves and to expand intravascular stents; their use carries procedure-related risks such as vessel injury, dissection, or distal embolization.

name: Balloon valvuloplasty
definition: A catheter-based procedure in which an inflatable balloon is positioned across a stenotic heart valve and expanded to separate fused or stiffened valve leaflets and enlarge the valve opening.
clinical_significance: Balloon valvuloplasty reduces obstruction to forward blood flow and can improve haemodynamics in selected valve stenoses; restenosis or new valve regurgitation may occur after the procedure.

name: Beta-blocker
definition: A medicine that blocks beta-adrenergic receptors, reducing the effects of epinephrine and norepinephrine on the heart and, for some agents, on vascular smooth muscle and the kidneys.
clinical_significance: Beta-blockade can slow the heart rate, reduce contractility and myocardial oxygen demand, suppress some arrhythmias, and lower blood pressure; excessive effect may cause bradycardia, hypotension, or impaired conduction.

name: Biopsy
definition: The removal of a small sample of cells or tissue by needle, endoscopic, catheter-based, or surgical technique for microscopic, biochemical, or molecular examination.
clinical_significance: Biopsy provides direct tissue evidence for diagnosing inflammation, infection, malignancy, or other structural disease; in heart transplantation it can also be used to assess myocardial rejection.

name: Blalock-Taussig procedure
definition: A palliative systemic-to-pulmonary artery shunt, classically connecting the subclavian artery to a pulmonary artery and often performed with a synthetic graft, to increase pulmonary blood flow in cyanotic congenital heart disease.
clinical_significance: The procedure can improve arterial oxygenation and support pulmonary blood flow before definitive congenital-heart repair; shunt obstruction, thrombosis, or excessive pulmonary flow are important potential complications.

name: Blood clot
definition: A semisolid mass formed when platelets, fibrin, and blood cells aggregate during coagulation. A clot may form normally to stop bleeding or abnormally within a blood vessel or heart chamber, where it is called a thrombus.
clinical_significance: Pathological thrombosis can obstruct venous or arterial blood flow or detach as an embolus, causing conditions such as deep-vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke.

name: Blood pressure
definition: The pressure exerted by circulating blood against the walls of the arteries, produced by the interaction of cardiac output and vascular resistance and expressed as systolic and diastolic values.
clinical_significance: Blood pressure is a major indicator of circulatory function; persistent elevation increases vascular and cardiac workload and risk of organ damage, whereas abnormally low pressure may impair tissue perfusion.

name: Blue babies
definition: A colloquial term for infants with central cyanosis, a bluish discoloration of the skin or mucous membranes caused by reduced arterial oxygenation or, less commonly, an abnormal haemoglobin.
clinical_significance: Cyanosis in an infant may indicate a cyanotic congenital heart defect, pulmonary disease, abnormal circulation, or a blood disorder and signifies potentially inadequate oxygen delivery to tissues.

name: Body mass index (BMI)
definition: A weight-to-height index calculated as body weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared (kg/m²). It is a population-level screening measure of weight status, not a direct measurement of body-fat percentage.
clinical_significance: Higher BMI is associated with increased risk of hypertension, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and other obesity-related conditions, but interpretation should account for body composition, age, and clinical context.

name: Bradycardia
definition: A heart rate that is slower than expected for the clinical context, commonly defined as fewer than 60 beats per minute in an adult at rest; it may result from slow sinus-node activity or impaired conduction.
clinical_significance: Bradycardia may be a normal physiological finding in sleep or trained athletes, but symptomatic or pathological bradycardia can reduce cardiac output and cause fatigue, dizziness, syncope, or exercise intolerance.

name: Bridge to transplant
definition: A treatment strategy in which mechanical circulatory support, such as a ventricular-assist device, maintains or supplements cardiac output in a patient with advanced heart failure until heart transplantation can be performed.
clinical_significance: Bridge support can stabilize circulation and preserve end-organ function while a patient awaits a donor heart; device-related infection, thrombosis, bleeding, and stroke remain important complications.

name: Bruit
definition: An abnormal sound heard over an artery with a stethoscope, produced by turbulent blood flow, often near a narrowed, irregular, or otherwise abnormal segment of the vessel.
clinical_significance: A bruit, such as a carotid bruit, can suggest underlying arterial stenosis or altered vascular flow, although it is not a definitive measure of the severity of obstruction and must be interpreted with other findings.

name: Bundle branch block
definition: A delay or interruption of electrical conduction through the right or left bundle branch, causing the corresponding ventricle to depolarize later than the other ventricle.
clinical_significance: Bundle branch block produces characteristic electrocardiographic changes and may be an incidental finding or a marker of underlying structural heart disease; a left bundle branch block can also cause ventricular dyssynchrony and worsen pump dysfunction.

name: Bypass
definition: A surgical procedure that creates an alternative route for blood flow around a narrowed or occluded artery, using a vein, an artery, or a synthetic graft as the conduit.
clinical_significance: Arterial bypass can restore perfusion beyond an obstructed segment, such as in coronary artery bypass grafting or peripheral revascularization, although graft failure, thrombosis, and operative complications can occur.

name: Calcium channel blocker (or calcium blocker)
definition: A medicine that blocks L-type calcium channels in vascular smooth muscle and, depending on the drug, in cardiac muscle and the conduction system.
clinical_significance: Calcium channel blockers can lower arterial pressure through vasodilation; non-dihydropyridine agents also slow atrioventricular conduction and reduce heart rate, making the class relevant to hypertension, angina, and selected tachyarrhythmias.

name: Capillaries
definition: The smallest blood vessels, linking arterioles with venules and consisting primarily of a single endothelial layer through which gases, nutrients, fluid, and metabolic waste can be exchanged with tissues.
clinical_significance: Capillary exchange supplies tissues with oxygen and nutrients and removes waste; altered capillary pressure or permeability contributes to oedema, impaired tissue oxygenation, and microvascular injury.

name: Cardiac
definition: An adjective meaning related to the heart, including its chambers, valves, myocardium, pericardium, electrical conduction system, or function.
clinical_significance: The term identifies a finding, disease, test, or procedure as involving the heart and helps distinguish cardiac pathology from disorders of other parts of the cardiovascular system.

name: Cardiac amyloidosis
definition: An infiltrative cardiomyopathy in which misfolded amyloid proteins, commonly light-chain or transthyretin amyloid, deposit in the myocardial interstitium and sometimes the conduction system.
clinical_significance: Amyloid infiltration makes the ventricles stiff and can cause restrictive physiology, heart failure, atrial or ventricular arrhythmias, and conduction disease; the amyloid type has important diagnostic and prognostic implications.

name: Cardiac arrest
definition: The abrupt cessation of effective cardiac mechanical activity, usually caused by ventricular fibrillation, ventricular tachycardia, or asystole.
clinical_significance: Cardiac arrest stops systemic perfusion and causes loss of consciousness and death without prompt restoration of circulation; it is distinct from myocardial infarction, although infarction can precipitate it.

name: Cardiac cachexia
definition: A wasting syndrome of involuntary weight loss, muscle depletion, and weakness associated with advanced chronic heart failure or other severe cardiac disease.
clinical_significance: It reflects systemic consequences of severe cardiac dysfunction and is associated with reduced functional reserve, poorer tolerance of illness, and adverse prognosis.

name: Cardiac catheterization
definition: A procedure in which a thin catheter is advanced through a blood vessel into the heart or great vessels for measurement, imaging, electrophysiological testing, or treatment.
clinical_significance: It permits direct assessment of intracardiac pressures and anatomy and provides access for angiography, biopsy, ablation, and catheter-based interventions.

name: Cardiac enzymes
definition: Proteins released from injured cells that catalyse biochemical reactions; in cardiovascular practice the term commonly refers to blood biomarkers such as cardiac troponin and, historically, CK-MB.
clinical_significance: Serial cardiac biomarker measurements help detect myocardial injury, although an elevated result must be interpreted with symptoms, ECG findings, and other causes of injury.

name: Cardiac output
definition: The volume of blood ejected by a ventricle into the circulation each minute, calculated as heart rate multiplied by stroke volume.
clinical_significance: It describes the heart’s global pumping performance; inadequate output can cause tissue hypoperfusion, while assessment of output helps characterise shock and heart failure.

name: Cardiologist
definition: A physician specialising in the prevention, diagnosis, and medical or catheter-based management of diseases of the heart and cardiovascular system.
clinical_significance: Cardiologists evaluate disorders such as coronary disease, arrhythmia, valve disease, and heart failure and may perform invasive diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.

name: Cardiology
definition: The medical specialty concerned with the structure, function, diseases, and treatment of the heart and circulatory system.
clinical_significance: It encompasses cardiovascular prevention, diagnostic testing, medicines, electrophysiology, catheter intervention, and management of acute and chronic heart disease.

name: Cardiomegaly
definition: Enlargement of the heart detected clinically or on imaging, without specifying its cause.
clinical_significance: It can reflect chronic pressure or volume overload, cardiomyopathy, athletic remodelling, or other disease; the underlying cause determines its clinical importance.

name: Cardiomyopathy
definition: A disease of the myocardium that alters the heart’s structure or function and is not solely explained by abnormal loading conditions or coronary disease.
clinical_significance: Cardiomyopathy may cause systolic or diastolic dysfunction, heart failure, arrhythmia, thromboembolism, or sudden death, with implications for family evaluation in inherited forms.

name: Cardiopulmonary bypass
definition: A technique in which a pump-oxygenator temporarily diverts and oxygenates venous blood and returns it to the arterial circulation while the heart is stopped or operating minimally.
clinical_significance: It provides a motionless, bloodless field for many open-heart operations but exposes the patient to inflammatory, bleeding, neurological, and organ-perfusion complications.

name: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR)
definition: Emergency chest compressions, with or without rescue breaths, used to provide artificial circulation and ventilation during cardiac arrest.
clinical_significance: CPR temporarily supports cerebral and coronary perfusion until spontaneous circulation is restored or definitive resuscitation is completed.

name: Cardiovascular (CV)
definition: Relating to the heart and blood vessels, including the arterial, venous, and microvascular components of circulation.
clinical_significance: The term groups conditions, tests, and treatments involving the circulatory system rather than the heart alone.

name: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD)
definition: An umbrella term for disorders of the heart and blood vessels, including coronary disease, stroke, hypertension, heart failure, valve disease, and peripheral arterial disease.
clinical_significance: CVD affects blood flow, cardiac function, or both and is a major cause of disability and death across populations.

name: Cardioversion
definition: Restoration of sinus rhythm from an arrhythmia by a synchronised electrical shock or, in some settings, an antiarrhythmic medicine.
clinical_significance: Synchronised cardioversion can terminate selected atrial or other supraventricular tachyarrhythmias and is timed to avoid delivering a shock during ventricular repolarisation.

name: Carotid artery
definition: One of the paired arteries in the neck that supplies blood to the brain and related head structures.
clinical_significance: Carotid atherosclerosis or embolism can reduce cerebral perfusion and cause transient ischaemic attack or ischaemic stroke.

name: Cerebral embolism
definition: An embolus that travels to and obstructs an artery supplying the brain, often originating from the heart or a proximal artery.
clinical_significance: It can abruptly interrupt focal cerebral blood flow and cause an ischaemic stroke, with the neurological deficit depending on the vessel involved.

name: Cerebral hemorrhage
definition: Bleeding into brain tissue or an intracranial compartment after rupture of a cerebral vessel.
clinical_significance: Intracranial bleeding can raise pressure, injure neural tissue, and cause sudden neurological deficit; hypertension and vascular malformations are important causes.

name: Cerebral thrombosis
definition: Formation of a thrombus within an artery supplying the brain, causing local obstruction of cerebral blood flow.
clinical_significance: The resulting ischaemia can produce an arterial ischaemic stroke, with severity determined by the vessel, collateral supply, and duration of occlusion.

name: Cerebrovascular
definition: Relating to the blood vessels supplying the brain and the circulation through those vessels.
clinical_significance: The term is used for diseases and investigations involving cerebral perfusion, including stroke, aneurysm, and vascular malformation.

name: Cerebrovascular accident
definition: A stroke: acute neurological dysfunction caused by interruption of cerebral blood flow through infarction or by intracranial haemorrhage.
clinical_significance: It identifies a time-critical form of brain injury that may cause permanent disability or death; the vascular mechanism guides diagnostic classification.

name: Cerebrovascular occlusion
definition: Blockage of an artery or other blood vessel supplying the brain, usually by thrombosis, embolism, or atherosclerotic disease.
clinical_significance: Occlusion reduces downstream cerebral perfusion and can produce focal ischaemia, infarction, and neurological deficits.

name: Cholesterol
definition: A sterol required for cell membranes, steroid hormones, and bile acids that circulates in blood within lipoprotein particles.
clinical_significance: Excess atherogenic cholesterol can accumulate in arterial walls and contribute to plaque formation and coronary, cerebral, or peripheral arterial disease.

name: Cineangiography
definition: X-ray fluoroscopy that records moving images of contrast passing through cardiac chambers or blood vessels.
clinical_significance: It displays the timing and pattern of blood flow and helps define coronary stenosis, vascular occlusion, and anatomy during catheter procedures.

name: Circulatory system
definition: The integrated system of the heart, blood vessels, and circulating blood that transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products.
clinical_significance: Its function determines tissue perfusion; failure of cardiac pumping or vascular integrity can produce shock, congestion, or organ ischaemia.

name: Claudication
definition: Reproducible aching, cramping, or fatigue in a limb during exertion that improves with rest, usually because arterial supply cannot meet muscle demand.
clinical_significance: Intermittent claudication is a typical symptom of peripheral arterial disease and indicates systemic atherosclerotic risk as well as impaired limb perfusion.

name: Collateral circulation
definition: An alternative network of vessels that supplies tissue when the usual arterial route is narrowed or blocked.
clinical_significance: Collateral flow can preserve perfusion and reduce ischaemic injury, but its adequacy affects symptoms and the consequences of arterial occlusion.

name: Computed tomography (CT or CAT scan)
definition: An imaging method that uses rotating X-rays and computer reconstruction to create cross-sectional or three-dimensional images.
clinical_significance: CT can rapidly assess coronary calcium, vascular anatomy, pulmonary embolism, aortic disease, and intracranial bleeding, depending on the protocol.

name: Conduction system
definition: Specialised cardiac tissue comprising the sinoatrial node, atrioventricular node, His bundle, bundle branches, and Purkinje fibres that generates and distributes electrical impulses.
clinical_significance: It coordinates atrial and ventricular contraction; disease in any component can produce bradycardia, block, dyssynchrony, or tachyarrhythmia.

name: Congenital
definition: Present at birth, whether caused by genetic factors, developmental disturbance, or an exposure during fetal development.
clinical_significance: Congenital cardiovascular abnormalities may involve cardiac chambers, valves, septa, or great vessels and can alter circulation from infancy or remain silent until adulthood.

name: Congenital heart defects
definition: Structural abnormalities of the heart or great vessels that arise during fetal development and are present at birth.
clinical_significance: Defects may create abnormal shunts, obstruction, or mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood and can lead to pulmonary hypertension, cyanosis, arrhythmia, or heart failure.

name: Congestive heart failure
definition: A clinical syndrome in which structural or functional cardiac abnormality causes inadequate output, elevated filling pressures, or both, producing symptoms such as breathlessness and fluid retention.
clinical_significance: Heart failure can cause pulmonary or systemic congestion, renal dysfunction, exercise limitation, and recurrent hospitalisation; ejection fraction and filling physiology help classify it.

name: Coronary arteries
definition: The right and left arteries arising from the aortic root that supply oxygenated blood to the myocardium and the cardiac conduction tissues.
clinical_significance: Narrowing or occlusion of a coronary artery causes myocardial ischaemia and can produce angina, infarction, ventricular dysfunction, or arrhythmia.

name: Coronary artery anomaly (CAA)
definition: A congenital abnormal origin, course, structure, or termination of a coronary artery.
clinical_significance: Some anomalies are incidental, whereas an abnormal course or narrowed origin can impair myocardial perfusion, cause ischaemia, or increase sudden-death risk during exertion.

name: Coronary artery bypass (CAB)
definition: A surgical revascularisation operation that uses arterial or venous grafts to route blood around obstructed coronary arteries.
clinical_significance: Bypass can restore flow to ischaemic myocardium when anatomy or disease burden makes catheter intervention unsuitable or less effective.

name: Coronary artery disease (CAD)
definition: Disease of the coronary arteries, most commonly caused by atherosclerotic plaque that narrows or obstructs their lumen.
clinical_significance: CAD can cause stable or acute myocardial ischaemia, angina, infarction, left-ventricular dysfunction, and sudden cardiac death.

name: Coronary heart disease
definition: Heart disease caused by atherosclerotic or other narrowing of the coronary arteries, reducing blood supply to the myocardium.
clinical_significance: It is a major cause of angina and myocardial infarction and may progress to heart failure or malignant arrhythmia.

name: Coronary occlusion
definition: Complete or near-complete blockage of a coronary artery or one of its branches.
clinical_significance: Acute occlusion can abruptly deprive myocardium of oxygen and cause myocardial infarction, whereas chronic occlusion may be partly compensated by collateral vessels.

name: Coronary thrombosis
definition: Formation of a thrombus within a coronary artery, often after rupture or erosion of an atherosclerotic plaque.
clinical_significance: The thrombus can obstruct myocardial blood flow and is a common mechanism of acute coronary syndrome and myocardial infarction.

name: Cryoablation
definition: Ablation technique that destroys selected tissue by applying extreme cold through a probe or catheter.
clinical_significance: Cardiac cryoablation can electrically isolate or eliminate arrhythmogenic tissue; lesion control and proximity to normal conduction tissue determine its risks and effectiveness.

name: Cyanosis
definition: Bluish discoloration of skin or mucous membranes caused by increased deoxygenated haemoglobin or an abnormal haemoglobin state.
clinical_significance: Central cyanosis may indicate inadequate arterial oxygenation from cardiac, pulmonary, or haemoglobin disease and signals altered oxygen delivery.

name: Cyanotic heart disease
definition: A congenital heart defect in which inadequate oxygenation or abnormal mixing allows relatively deoxygenated blood to reach the systemic circulation.
clinical_significance: It causes central cyanosis and may lead to chronic hypoxaemia, compensatory blood changes, pulmonary vascular disease, or impaired development.

name: Death rate (age-adjusted)
definition: A mortality rate statistically standardised to a reference age distribution so populations with different age structures can be compared.
clinical_significance: Age adjustment improves interpretation of cardiovascular mortality trends without confusing changes in population age with changes in disease risk.

name: Deep vein thrombosis
definition: A thrombus in a deep vein, usually of the lower limb, pelvis, or upper limb.
clinical_significance: DVT can obstruct venous return and embolise to the pulmonary arteries, causing pulmonary embolism; it also may lead to chronic venous symptoms.

name: Defibrillator
definition: A device that delivers an electrical shock to terminate certain life-threatening tachyarrhythmias, especially ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia.
clinical_significance: External defibrillation can restore an organised rhythm during arrest, while an implantable defibrillator can detect and treat recurrent malignant ventricular arrhythmias.

name: Diabetes (diabetes mellitus)
definition: A group of metabolic disorders characterised by chronic hyperglycaemia caused by inadequate insulin secretion, impaired insulin action, or both.
clinical_significance: Diabetes accelerates atherosclerosis and damages small vessels, increasing the risk of coronary disease, stroke, peripheral arterial disease, kidney disease, and heart failure.

name: Diastolic blood pressure
definition: The arterial pressure during ventricular relaxation, represented by the lower number in a blood-pressure measurement.
clinical_significance: It reflects arterial resistance and compliance during diastole; persistently elevated values contribute to vascular and cardiac injury, while very low values may impair coronary perfusion.

name: Digitalis
definition: A group of cardiac glycosides derived from Digitalis plants, including digoxin, that influence myocardial contraction and cardiac electrical conduction.
clinical_significance: Digitalis compounds have a narrow therapeutic range and may be used in selected heart-failure or atrial-fibrillation settings; toxicity can cause gastrointestinal, visual, or rhythm disturbances.

name: Dissecting aneurysm
definition: Aortic dissection, in which a tear in the inner aortic wall allows blood to track between wall layers and create a false lumen.
clinical_significance: Dissection can obstruct branch arteries, cause acute aortic regurgitation or tamponade, and rupture; its complications depend on location and extent.

name: Diuretic
definition: A medicine that increases renal sodium and water excretion, thereby reducing circulating volume and, in many cases, blood pressure.
clinical_significance: Diuretics relieve fluid congestion in heart failure and lower pressure, but excessive loss can cause hypotension, kidney dysfunction, or electrolyte disturbance.

name: Doppler ultrasound
definition: An ultrasound technique that estimates the direction and velocity of moving blood from changes in the reflected sound frequency.
clinical_significance: It evaluates arterial and venous flow, detects obstruction or reflux, and contributes to assessment of valve regurgitation and cardiac haemodynamics.

name: Dysarthria
definition: Impaired articulation caused by weakness, incoordination, or abnormal tone of the muscles used for speech, usually from neurological disease.
clinical_significance: Dysarthria can be a focal sign of stroke or other nervous-system injury and helps localise the functional consequences of cerebrovascular disease.

name: Dyspnea
definition: The subjective experience of difficult, uncomfortable, or inadequate breathing.
clinical_significance: Dyspnoea is common in pulmonary congestion and heart failure but is nonspecific; its exertional, positional, and resting patterns help distinguish cardiovascular causes.

name: Echocardiography
definition: Ultrasound imaging of the heart that produces moving views of chambers, valves, myocardium, blood flow, and haemodynamic function.
clinical_significance: It is central to evaluating ejection fraction, valve disease, chamber size, congenital defects, pericardial fluid, and intracardiac thrombus.

name: Edema
definition: Accumulation of excess fluid in the interstitial tissues, producing swelling.
clinical_significance: Peripheral oedema can reflect venous disease, renal or hepatic dysfunction, or right-sided heart failure; pulmonary oedema indicates fluid in the lungs and impaired gas exchange.

name: Ejection fraction
definition: The percentage of blood in a ventricle at end-diastole that is ejected during systole, calculated as stroke volume divided by end-diastolic volume.
clinical_significance: It helps classify ventricular systolic function and heart-failure phenotype, although a preserved value does not exclude impaired filling or elevated filling pressures.

name: Electrocardiogram (ECG or EKG)
definition: A recording of the heart’s electrical potentials from electrodes placed on the skin.
clinical_significance: An ECG can identify rhythm, conduction abnormalities, myocardial ischaemia or infarction, chamber effects, and electrolyte-related electrical changes.

name: Electroencephalogram (EEG)
definition: A recording of electrical activity in the brain using electrodes placed on the scalp.
clinical_significance: EEG helps distinguish seizures and other neurological causes from syncope, which may result from transient cardiovascular reduction in cerebral perfusion.

name: Electrophysiological study (EPS)
definition: An invasive test in which intracardiac electrodes record and stimulate cardiac electrical activity through catheters.
clinical_significance: EPS can localise conduction abnormalities, identify arrhythmia mechanisms, assess sudden-death risk, and guide ablation or device decisions.

name: Embolus
definition: Material travelling through the bloodstream that can lodge in and obstruct a smaller vessel; it may be a thrombus, fat, air, or other material.
clinical_significance: Embolisation can cause sudden infarction of tissue supplied by the blocked artery, including stroke, pulmonary embolism, or limb ischaemia.

name: Endarterectomy
definition: Surgical removal of atherosclerotic plaque and associated obstructive material from the inner surface of an artery.
clinical_significance: Carotid endarterectomy can improve cerebral arterial patency in selected stenosis, while peripheral procedures can restore limb blood flow.

name: Endocardium
definition: The thin endothelial lining of the heart chambers and the surfaces of the heart valves.
clinical_significance: Endocardial injury or infection can promote thrombus and vegetation formation and may impair valve function or cardiac conduction.

name: Endothelium
definition: A layer of specialised cells lining blood vessels and the inner surface of the heart.
clinical_significance: Endothelial dysfunction promotes vasoconstriction, inflammation, platelet activation, and atherosclerosis and is therefore important in vascular disease.

name: Endocarditis
definition: Inflammation and infection of the endocardium, most often involving a heart valve and caused by bacteria or fungi.
clinical_significance: Endocarditis can destroy valves, cause regurgitation and heart failure, and generate emboli or immune-mediated organ injury.

name: Enlarged heart
definition: A descriptive term for a heart whose chambers or muscular walls are larger than expected for body size and clinical context.
clinical_significance: Cardiac enlargement may be adaptive or pathological and can reflect hypertension, valve disease, cardiomyopathy, or chronic volume overload.

name: Enzyme
definition: A protein or RNA molecule that accelerates a specific biochemical reaction without being consumed by that reaction.
clinical_significance: Measurement of particular enzymes or enzyme-associated biomarkers can provide evidence of tissue injury, although cardiac troponin is now preferred for myocardial injury assessment.

name: Epicardium
definition: The thin outer layer of the heart wall, formed by the visceral layer of the serous pericardium and covering the myocardium.
clinical_significance: The epicardium contributes to the protective pericardial surface and may be involved in inflammation, adhesions, or epicardial fat-related disease.

name: Estrogen
definition: A group of steroid hormones, including oestradiol, involved in reproductive biology and effects on multiple tissues.
clinical_significance: Oestrogen status influences vascular biology and lipid patterns, but endogenous or replacement hormone effects do not eliminate conventional cardiovascular risk factors.

name: Estrogen (or hormone) replacement therapy (ERT or HRT)
definition: Treatment using oestrogen alone or oestrogen with a progestogen to replace hormones or relieve menopausal symptoms.
clinical_significance: Hormone therapy has complex cardiovascular effects that vary with age, timing, formulation, and vascular history and is not a treatment for preventing cardiovascular disease.

name: Exercise stress test
definition: A test that increases cardiac workload through exercise while monitoring ECG, symptoms, blood pressure, and sometimes imaging or perfusion.
clinical_significance: It can reveal inducible myocardial ischaemia, exercise-related arrhythmia, functional capacity, or an abnormal blood-pressure response.

name: Familial hypercholesterolemia
definition: An inherited disorder, usually involving impaired LDL-receptor pathway function, causing markedly increased low-density lipoprotein cholesterol from an early age.
clinical_significance: Prolonged exposure to high LDL cholesterol accelerates premature atherosclerosis and coronary disease; the diagnosis also has implications for relatives.

name: Fatty acids (fats)
definition: Organic molecules that form important components of dietary and stored fat and differ according to chain length and degree of saturation.
clinical_significance: Fatty-acid composition influences lipoprotein concentrations and atherosclerotic risk, although cardiovascular effects depend on the food source and overall dietary pattern.

name: Fibrillation
definition: Rapid, chaotic, uncoordinated electrical activity and contraction of individual cardiac muscle fibres, preventing the chamber from contracting effectively as a unit.
clinical_significance: Atrial fibrillation promotes irregular ventricular activation and thromboembolism, whereas ventricular fibrillation causes cardiac arrest through loss of effective output.

name: First-degree heart block
definition: Prolongation of conduction time from the atria to the ventricles, seen as a prolonged PR interval on ECG, without dropped ventricular beats.
clinical_significance: It is often asymptomatic but may indicate conduction-system disease or drug effect and can progress when associated with more extensive conduction abnormality.

name: Flutter
definition: A rapid, relatively organised repetitive electrical circuit producing fast contractions of a cardiac chamber, especially the atria.
clinical_significance: Atrial flutter can cause rapid ventricular response, reduced filling, and thromboembolic risk, while its organised circuit may make it amenable to catheter ablation.

name: Fusiform aneurysm
definition: An aneurysm that expands around the full circumference of a longitudinal segment of an artery, producing a spindle-shaped enlargement.
clinical_significance: Its size and location determine the risks of thrombosis, distal embolisation, compression, dissection, or rupture.

name: Gated blood pool scan
definition: A radionuclide study that tracks labelled red blood cells through the cardiac chambers in synchrony with the ECG.
clinical_significance: It can quantify ventricular ejection fraction and regional wall motion, providing a reproducible assessment of pump function.

name: Genetic testing
definition: Laboratory analysis of DNA or other genetic material to identify inherited variants associated with disease or disease susceptibility.
clinical_significance: Testing can clarify inherited cardiomyopathy or arrhythmia syndromes, guide family screening, and help interpret unexplained sudden death.

name: Guidewire
definition: A flexible wire introduced through a vessel to provide a pathway and support for advancing a catheter or other endovascular device.
clinical_significance: It enables precise access during angioplasty, stenting, and other interventions; vessel perforation, dissection, or arrhythmia are procedural risks.

name: Heart assist device
definition: A mechanical circulatory-support device that helps a weakened ventricle move blood through the pulmonary or systemic circulation.
clinical_significance: It can support patients with severe heart failure as a bridge to transplantation, recovery, or longer-term therapy, but infection, bleeding, and thrombosis are important complications.

name: Heart attack
definition: Acute myocardial infarction: injury or death of heart muscle caused by an imbalance between myocardial oxygen supply and demand, most often from acute coronary obstruction.
clinical_significance: It can impair ventricular function and cause heart failure, arrhythmia, shock, or death; ECG and cardiac biomarkers establish its clinical classification.

name: Heart block
definition: Delayed or absent conduction of electrical impulses through the atrioventricular node or His–Purkinje system.
clinical_significance: The resulting bradycardia or loss of atrioventricular synchrony can reduce cardiac output, cause syncope, and in advanced forms lead to life-threatening pauses.

name: Heart failure
definition: A clinical syndrome in which the heart cannot provide adequate output or can do so only with abnormally high filling pressures.
clinical_significance: It causes breathlessness, fatigue, congestion, and organ dysfunction and may result from ischaemic, valvular, hypertensive, genetic, or other myocardial disease.

name: Heart-lung machine
definition: A pump-oxygenator that temporarily takes over circulation and gas exchange during operations in which the heart is opened or stopped.
clinical_significance: It enables cardiopulmonary bypass and complex cardiac surgery but can contribute to bleeding, inflammation, embolism, and transient organ dysfunction.

name: Hematocrit
definition: The proportion of whole-blood volume occupied by red blood cells, usually reported as a percentage or fraction.
clinical_significance: It helps assess anaemia, polycythaemia, and haemoconcentration; abnormal viscosity or oxygen-carrying capacity can affect cardiovascular workload and perfusion.

name: Hemochromatosis
definition: A disorder of excessive iron absorption and deposition in tissues, caused by inherited or acquired abnormalities of iron regulation.
clinical_significance: Iron deposition in the myocardium can cause dilated or restrictive cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia, and heart failure, while phlebotomy-related anaemia can also affect circulation.

name: Heredity
definition: The transmission of genetic information and traits from parents to offspring.
clinical_significance: Inherited variants can predispose to cardiomyopathy, arrhythmia, lipid disorders, congenital defects, and premature vascular disease, making family history clinically relevant.

name: High blood pressure
definition: Persistently elevated arterial blood pressure above accepted diagnostic thresholds, also called hypertension.
clinical_significance: Chronic pressure overload promotes left-ventricular hypertrophy, arterial disease, kidney injury, stroke, heart failure, and coronary disease.

name: High density lipoprotein (HDL)
definition: A lipoprotein particle that transports cholesterol and other lipids between tissues and the liver.
clinical_significance: HDL concentration is associated with cardiovascular risk, but it is not by itself a direct measure of protective HDL function and should not be interpreted in isolation.

name: Holter monitor
definition: A portable ambulatory ECG recorder that continuously or intermittently records cardiac electrical activity, commonly for 24 hours or longer.
clinical_significance: It helps correlate intermittent palpitations, dizziness, or syncope with arrhythmia and assesses rhythm burden that a brief ECG may miss.

name: Homocysteine
definition: A sulphur-containing amino acid formed during methionine metabolism and normally present in blood at low concentrations.
clinical_significance: Marked elevation can accompany nutritional or inherited metabolic disorders and is associated with vascular risk, although it is not a specific diagnostic test for coronary disease.

name: Hypertension
definition: A chronic disorder in which arterial blood pressure is persistently elevated according to validated office, home, or ambulatory measurements.
clinical_significance: It causes progressive vascular and cardiac damage and substantially increases the risk of stroke, coronary disease, kidney disease, atrial fibrillation, and heart failure.

name: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM)
definition: A form of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in which excessive myocardial thickening, often of the septum, obstructs left-ventricular outflow.
clinical_significance: The obstruction and abnormal myocardium can cause exertional symptoms, mitral regurgitation, atrial or ventricular arrhythmia, and sudden cardiac death.

name: Hypertrophy
definition: An enlargement of cells or tissue caused by increased cell size rather than increased cell number.
clinical_significance: Cardiac hypertrophy commonly develops in response to pressure or volume overload and can initially compensate but later impair relaxation, perfusion, and electrical stability.

name: Hyperventilation
definition: Ventilation that exceeds the body’s metabolic need for carbon dioxide elimination, lowering arterial carbon dioxide concentration.
clinical_significance: It can cause light-headedness, tingling, and chest discomfort and may complicate assessment of dyspnoea, but it is not synonymous with adequate oxygenation.

name: Hypoglycemia
definition: An abnormally low blood-glucose concentration capable of producing autonomic and neurological symptoms.
clinical_significance: It can provoke adrenergic tachycardia, blood-pressure changes, arrhythmia, and impaired consciousness, particularly in people receiving glucose-lowering treatment.

name: Hypokinesia
definition: Reduced movement or contraction of tissue; in cardiology it commonly describes diminished myocardial wall motion.
clinical_significance: Regional cardiac hypokinesia can indicate ischaemia or infarction, while global hypokinesia suggests diffuse ventricular dysfunction.

name: Hypotension
definition: Arterial blood pressure that is abnormally low for the person’s clinical context or insufficient to maintain organ perfusion.
clinical_significance: It may result from low output, vasodilation, volume loss, or arrhythmia and can cause syncope, myocardial ischaemia, kidney injury, or shock.

name: Hypoxia
definition: Insufficient oxygen availability or utilisation at tissue level, often due to low arterial oxygenation, reduced blood flow, or impaired cellular use.
clinical_significance: Hypoxia stresses the heart and brain and may result from pulmonary disease, cyanotic heart disease, anaemia, or circulatory failure.

name: Idiopathic
definition: Describing a disease or finding for which no cause has been identified after appropriate evaluation.
clinical_significance: The label indicates unresolved aetiology rather than a distinct mechanism and may change if later genetic, inflammatory, toxic, or structural evidence emerges.

name: Immunosuppressants
definition: Medicines that reduce immune-system activity through effects on lymphocytes, cytokines, or other immune pathways.
clinical_significance: They prevent rejection after heart transplantation and treat selected inflammatory disease, but increase susceptibility to infection and can have renal, metabolic, or cardiovascular effects.

name: Impedance plethysmography
definition: A non-invasive method that detects changes in electrical impedance produced by variations in blood volume within a limb.
clinical_significance: It can assess venous outflow and help detect haemodynamic consequences of deep-vein obstruction, although ultrasound is commonly used for direct DVT imaging.

name: Incompetent valve
definition: A heart valve that fails to close completely, allowing blood to flow backwards during the phase when it should be sealed; also called valve regurgitation or insufficiency.
clinical_significance: Regurgitant flow creates volume overload and may enlarge chambers, cause symptoms, and eventually produce heart failure or pulmonary hypertension.

name: Infarct
definition: An area of tissue necrosis caused by prolonged interruption of its blood supply or, less commonly, impaired venous drainage.
clinical_significance: A myocardial infarct permanently reduces viable contractile tissue and may lead to scar, ventricular remodelling, heart failure, or arrhythmia.

name: Infective endocarditis
definition: Infection of the endocardial surface, usually a valve, by bacteria or fungi that form inflammatory vegetations.
clinical_significance: It can destroy valves, cause regurgitation and heart failure, seed emboli, and produce immune-complex injury in distant organs.

name: Inferior vena cava
definition: The large vein that returns deoxygenated blood from the lower limbs, pelvis, and abdomen to the right atrium.
clinical_significance: Obstruction or increased pressure in this vessel contributes to lower-body venous congestion, oedema, and collateral venous flow.

name: Inotropes
definition: Medicines that alter myocardial contractility; positive inotropes increase contraction strength, whereas negative inotropes reduce it.
clinical_significance: Positive inotropic support can raise cardiac output in selected low-output states, but increased myocardial oxygen demand and arrhythmia are important risks.

name: Internal mammary artery
definition: An artery running along the inner chest wall, also called the internal thoracic artery, that can be used as a coronary bypass graft.
clinical_significance: Its durable patency makes it an important conduit for revascularising the left anterior descending coronary artery.

name: Intravascular echocardiography
definition: Ultrasound imaging performed from within a vessel or cardiac structure using a miniature transducer on a catheter.
clinical_significance: It shows plaque, lumen dimensions, stent expansion, and vessel-wall anatomy, helping guide and assess coronary intervention.

name: Introducer sheath
definition: A short hollow tube placed through the wall of a blood vessel to maintain access for catheters and devices during an intervention.
clinical_significance: The sheath permits repeated catheter exchanges and stable access but can cause bleeding, haematoma, thrombosis, infection, or vessel injury.

name: Ischemia
definition: Inadequate blood flow and oxygen delivery to tissue, usually because arterial supply is narrowed or obstructed.
clinical_significance: Ischaemia can impair organ function and cause reversible symptoms or irreversible infarction; myocardial ischaemia produces angina and may trigger arrhythmia.

name: Ischemic heart disease
definition: Heart disease caused by inadequate myocardial blood supply, most often because of atherosclerotic narrowing or obstruction of the coronary arteries.
clinical_significance: It encompasses chronic coronary syndrome and acute coronary syndromes and may cause angina, infarction, ventricular dysfunction, or sudden death.

name: Ischemic stroke
definition: A stroke caused by cerebral infarction from arterial occlusion or critically reduced blood flow, without primary intracranial bleeding.
clinical_significance: It produces focal neurological dysfunction and may result from thrombosis, embolism, or small-vessel disease; the mechanism influences diagnostic evaluation.

name: Jugular veins
definition: The major veins in the neck that drain blood from the head, brain, face, and neck into the brachiocephalic veins and superior vena cava.
clinical_significance: Jugular venous pressure and waveform provide bedside information about right-atrial pressure and systemic venous congestion.

name: Left ventricular assist device (LVAD)
definition: A mechanical pump that draws blood from the left ventricle and delivers it to the aorta, supporting systemic circulation.
clinical_significance: An LVAD can provide temporary or long-term support in advanced heart failure, but bleeding, thrombosis, infection, stroke, and right-heart failure are recognised complications.

name: Lesion
definition: A localised area of abnormal tissue caused by injury, inflammation, degeneration, infection, neoplasia, or another disease process.
clinical_significance: In cardiovascular medicine the term may describe a plaque, stenosis, infarct, mass, or other focal abnormality whose location and nature determine its significance.

name: Lipid
definition: A group of water-insoluble or poorly soluble organic substances that includes cholesterol, triglycerides, phospholipids, and fatty acids.
clinical_significance: Lipid transport and metabolism influence atherosclerotic plaque formation, energy storage, and cardiovascular risk.

name: Lipoprotein
definition: A particle composed of lipids and proteins that transports otherwise water-insoluble fats through blood and lymph.
clinical_significance: Different lipoproteins have different relationships to atherosclerosis; LDL particles are a major source of cholesterol delivered to arterial walls.

name: Low density lipoprotein (LDL)
definition: A lipoprotein particle that carries cholesterol from the liver to peripheral tissues and can enter the arterial wall.
clinical_significance: Cumulative exposure to elevated LDL cholesterol promotes atherosclerotic plaque and is causally related to coronary, cerebral, and peripheral arterial disease.

name: Lumen
definition: The internal channel of a tubular structure, such as a blood vessel, heart chamber, or valve opening, through which fluid passes.
clinical_significance: Lumen diameter determines resistance to flow; narrowing or occlusion reduces downstream perfusion and may cause ischaemia.

name: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
definition: An imaging technique using magnetic fields and radiofrequency signals to create detailed images without ionising radiation.
clinical_significance: Cardiac MRI characterises myocardium, scar, inflammation, perfusion, masses, vessels, and ventricular function and can clarify diagnoses not resolved by ultrasound.

name: Maze surgery
definition: A surgical arrhythmia procedure that creates a pattern of atrial incisions or lesions to interrupt re-entry and direct electrical impulses towards the atrioventricular node.
clinical_significance: The Maze procedure can reduce persistent atrial fibrillation and restore coordinated atrial rhythm, often when performed with other cardiac surgery.

name: Mitral stenosis
definition: Narrowing of the mitral-valve orifice that obstructs blood flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle during diastole.
clinical_significance: It raises left-atrial and pulmonary pressures, causing breathlessness, atrial enlargement, atrial fibrillation, thromboembolism, and eventually right-sided failure.

name: Mitral valve
definition: The atrioventricular valve between the left atrium and left ventricle, consisting of two leaflets supported by chordae and papillary muscles.
clinical_significance: It ensures one-way flow into the left ventricle; stenosis or regurgitation can cause atrial and ventricular remodelling and heart failure.

name: Mitral valve prolapse
definition: Displacement of one or both mitral leaflets into the left atrium during ventricular systole, sometimes with associated regurgitation.
clinical_significance: It is often benign but can produce mitral regurgitation, endocarditis risk in selected contexts, ventricular arrhythmia, or rarely sudden death.

name: Mitral valve regurgitation
definition: Backward leakage of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium during systole because the mitral valve does not close effectively.
clinical_significance: Chronic regurgitation causes left-atrial and ventricular volume overload, whereas acute severe regurgitation can rapidly cause pulmonary oedema and low output.

name: mm Hg
definition: A unit of pressure equal to one millimetre of mercury, commonly used for blood pressure and intracardiac pressure measurements.
clinical_significance: The unit standardises reporting of arterial, venous, and chamber pressures used to diagnose hypertension, valve disease, and haemodynamic failure.

name: Monounsaturated fats
definition: Dietary fatty acids containing one carbon-carbon double bond, found in foods such as olive oil, nuts, seeds, and avocados.
clinical_significance: Replacing saturated or trans fats with unsaturated fats generally improves the lipid profile and may reduce cardiovascular risk within an overall healthy dietary pattern.

name: Mortality
definition: The occurrence or rate of death in a defined population during a specified period, often attributed to a disease or cause.
clinical_significance: Cardiovascular mortality measures the fatal burden of heart and vascular disease and helps compare prognosis and population health over time.

name: Murmur
definition: An additional audible sound produced by turbulent blood flow through the heart or great vessels, heard during cardiac auscultation.
clinical_significance: A murmur may indicate valve stenosis, regurgitation, a congenital shunt, or increased flow, but its timing and quality are needed for interpretation.

name: Myocardial infarction
definition: Irreversible injury and necrosis of heart muscle caused by acute or prolonged myocardial ischaemia.
clinical_significance: It can reduce ventricular function and cause arrhythmia, mechanical complications, heart failure, or death; ECG, symptoms, and troponin establish the diagnosis.

name: Myocardial ischemia
definition: A state in which the myocardium receives insufficient oxygenated blood for its metabolic demand.
clinical_significance: It may cause angina, ECG changes, ventricular dysfunction, or arrhythmia and can progress to infarction if prolonged.

name: Myocarditis
definition: Inflammatory disease of the heart muscle caused by infection, immune-mediated injury, toxins, or other systemic processes.
clinical_significance: Myocarditis can cause chest pain, ventricular dysfunction, heart failure, conduction disease, arrhythmia, and sudden death; inflammation may be focal or diffuse.

name: Myocardium
definition: The muscular middle layer of the heart wall, composed of cardiac muscle cells that contract and relax rhythmically.
clinical_significance: Myocardial injury or remodelling affects systolic function, filling, electrical stability, and the ability to maintain cardiac output.

name: Myxomatous degeneration
definition: A degenerative change in valve connective tissue in which extracellular matrix accumulates and the leaflets become thickened, redundant, and less structurally resilient.
clinical_significance: It commonly underlies mitral valve prolapse and can cause progressive mitral regurgitation, chamber enlargement, and arrhythmia.

name: Nitroglycerin
definition: A nitrate medicine that releases nitric oxide and relaxes vascular smooth muscle, particularly reducing venous return and dilating coronary vessels.
clinical_significance: It relieves myocardial ischaemic chest pain by reducing cardiac preload and oxygen demand; its effects include hypotension and headache.

name: Necrosis
definition: Unregulated death of cells or tissue caused by severe injury, ischaemia, infection, toxins, or other pathological processes.
clinical_significance: Myocardial necrosis defines infarction and leaves scar tissue that can impair contraction and provide a substrate for ventricular arrhythmia.

name: Noninvasive procedures
definition: Diagnostic or therapeutic procedures performed without inserting an instrument through the skin or into a body cavity or blood vessel.
clinical_significance: Non-invasive cardiovascular tests such as ECG, echocardiography, and external monitoring provide information without the vascular and procedural risks of catheterisation.

name: NSTEMI
definition: A non-ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction, defined by acute myocardial injury with clinical evidence of ischaemia but without persistent ST elevation meeting STEMI criteria.
clinical_significance: NSTEMI represents acute coronary syndrome and may result from partial occlusion or severe supply-demand imbalance; risk assessment guides its classification and management.

name: Obesity
definition: A chronic disease characterised by excessive adiposity that may impair health and is commonly assessed with body-mass index alongside clinical measures.
clinical_significance: Obesity promotes hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidaemia, sleep apnoea, inflammation, and structural cardiac changes, increasing cardiovascular risk.

name: Occluded artery
definition: An artery whose lumen is completely or substantially blocked by thrombus, plaque, embolus, dissection, or another process.
clinical_significance: Occlusion can critically reduce downstream perfusion and produce acute or chronic ischaemia, infarction, or tissue loss depending on collateral supply.

name: Open heart surgery
definition: Surgery in which the heart is directly exposed through a chest incision, often with cardiopulmonary bypass and sometimes with the heart stopped.
clinical_significance: It allows repair or replacement of valves, correction of congenital defects, and coronary bypass but carries operative risks involving bleeding, infection, stroke, and organ dysfunction.

name: Pacemaker
definition: An implanted device that senses cardiac activity and delivers timed electrical impulses when the intrinsic rhythm is too slow or conduction is impaired.
clinical_significance: Pacemakers restore rate or atrioventricular coordination in symptomatic bradycardia and heart block and can improve cardiac output and prevent pauses.

name: Palpitation
definition: An individual’s awareness of the heartbeat as pounding, racing, fluttering, skipping, or irregular.
clinical_significance: Palpitations may accompany benign ectopic beats, sustained arrhythmia, anxiety, anaemia, or thyroid disease; ECG correlation is needed to identify the cause.

name: Pancreas
definition: A gland behind the stomach that produces digestive enzymes and hormones, including insulin and glucagon, which regulate blood glucose.
clinical_significance: Pancreatic endocrine dysfunction can cause diabetes, a major risk factor for atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease.

name: Pancreatitis
definition: Inflammation of the pancreas, which may be acute or chronic and commonly results from gallstones, alcohol, metabolic disease, or medications.
clinical_significance: Severe pancreatitis can cause systemic inflammation, fluid shifts, hypotension, and cardiac stress, while chronic disease may contribute to diabetes and nutritional decline.

name: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT)
definition: A sudden-onset, sudden-termination episode of rapid regular tachycardia arising above the ventricles, usually through re-entry involving the atrioventricular node or an accessory pathway.
clinical_significance: Episodes can cause palpitations, dizziness, chest discomfort, or hypotension; recurrent rapid rates may impair ventricular function.

name: Patent ductus arteriosus
definition: Persistent communication between the descending aorta and pulmonary artery after birth, when the ductus arteriosus should have closed.
clinical_significance: A significant left-to-right shunt can cause pulmonary overcirculation, left-heart volume overload, pulmonary hypertension, and eventually reversed cyanotic flow.

name: Patent foramen ovale
definition: A persistent flap-like communication between the right and left atria caused by incomplete postnatal fusion of the fetal foramen ovale.
clinical_significance: It is usually haemodynamically minor but can permit paradoxical embolism when right-atrial pressure rises and is relevant in selected otherwise unexplained strokes.

name: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)
definition: A catheter-based coronary revascularisation procedure, usually involving balloon dilation, stent implantation, or both.
clinical_significance: PCI can reopen or widen an obstructed coronary artery in acute or chronic ischaemia and restore myocardial perfusion without open surgery.

name: Percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA)
definition: A catheter procedure that advances a balloon across a coronary stenosis and inflates it to enlarge the arterial lumen; it is an older term for balloon coronary angioplasty.
clinical_significance: PTCA restores coronary flow but may cause dissection or recoil and is now commonly combined with stent placement to reduce restenosis.

name: Pericarditis
definition: Inflammation of the pericardial sac surrounding the heart, caused by infection, immune disease, infarction, malignancy, or other injury.
clinical_significance: It commonly causes positional chest pain and may produce pericardial effusion, constriction, or tamponade that impairs cardiac filling.

name: Pericardiocentesis
definition: A needle or catheter procedure that removes fluid or blood from the pericardial space surrounding the heart.
clinical_significance: It can relieve pressure in cardiac tamponade and provide fluid for diagnostic analysis, but myocardial or coronary injury and bleeding are procedural risks.

name: Pericardium
definition: A double-layered sac surrounding the heart, with a fibrous outer layer and a serous inner layer containing a small lubricating fluid volume.
clinical_significance: The pericardium limits acute distension and reduces friction; inflammation, fluid, or scarring can restrict cardiac filling.

name: Plaque
