definition: A focal accumulation of lipids, inflammatory cells, fibrous tissue, and sometimes calcium within an arterial wall, characteristic of atherosclerosis.
clinical_significance: Plaque can narrow the lumen or rupture and trigger thrombosis, causing coronary events, ischaemic stroke, or peripheral arterial disease.

name: Platelets
definition: Small anucleate blood-cell fragments derived from megakaryocytes that adhere, activate, and aggregate during haemostasis.
clinical_significance: Platelets are central to arterial thrombus formation and are targets of antiplatelet medicines used in coronary and cerebrovascular disease.

name: Polyunsaturated fat
definition: A fatty acid containing two or more carbon-carbon double bonds, found in many plant oils, nuts, seeds, and fish.
clinical_significance: Replacing saturated fat with polyunsaturated fat generally lowers LDL cholesterol and can reduce cardiovascular risk, depending on the dietary source.

name: Positron emission tomography (PET)
definition: A nuclear-imaging technique that detects positrons from an injected tracer to map tissue metabolism, perfusion, or viability.
clinical_significance: Cardiac PET can assess myocardial perfusion and viability and may help distinguish living but dysfunctional myocardium from scar.

name: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS)
definition: A form of orthostatic intolerance characterised by an excessive increase in heart rate after standing without sustained orthostatic hypotension as the defining feature.
clinical_significance: It can cause dizziness, palpitations, fatigue, and exercise intolerance through abnormal autonomic and circulatory responses to upright posture.

name: Premature ventricular contraction (PVC)
definition: An extra heartbeat arising prematurely from ventricular myocardium rather than the normal conduction pathway.
clinical_significance: Occasional PVCs may be benign, whereas frequent or complex PVCs can indicate structural disease, trigger ventricular tachycardia, or contribute to reversible cardiomyopathy.

name: Prevalence
definition: The proportion or number of people in a population who have a disease or condition at a specified time or during a specified period.
clinical_significance: Cardiovascular prevalence describes existing disease burden and helps estimate healthcare needs, but it differs from incidence, which measures new cases.

name: Pulmonary
definition: Relating to the lungs or pulmonary circulation between the right side of the heart and the lungs.
clinical_significance: Pulmonary disease or vascular pressure directly affects oxygenation, right-ventricular workload, and the symptoms of cardiovascular illness.

name: Pulmonary embolism
definition: Obstruction of a pulmonary artery or branch by material, most often a thrombus that has travelled from a deep vein.
clinical_significance: It can abruptly increase pulmonary vascular resistance, strain the right ventricle, impair oxygenation, and cause shock or death when extensive.

name: Pulmonary valve
definition: The semilunar valve between the right ventricle and pulmonary artery that opens during systole and closes during diastole.
clinical_significance: Pulmonary stenosis obstructs right-ventricular ejection, while regurgitation causes right-ventricular volume overload.

name: Pulmonary vein
definition: A vein that carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium; there are usually four major pulmonary veins.
clinical_significance: Pulmonary venous anatomy is important in left-atrial filling and in catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation; obstruction can cause pulmonary congestion.

name: Radial artery access
definition: A catheter-entry approach using the radial artery at the wrist rather than a femoral or other access vessel.
clinical_significance: It provides access for coronary angiography and PCI with generally lower access-site bleeding risk, although radial spasm or hand perfusion issues may occur.

name: Radionuclide imaging
definition: Imaging that detects radiation from a small administered radioactive tracer to show perfusion, metabolism, or organ function.
clinical_significance: Cardiovascular radionuclide studies can identify inducible ischaemia, infarction, ventricular function, or pulmonary embolism according to the tracer and protocol.

name: Radionuclide studies
definition: Diagnostic examinations that use radiopharmaceuticals and external detectors to display physiological processes or tissue distribution.
clinical_significance: They provide functional information about myocardial perfusion, viability, ventricular ejection, and pulmonary circulation that complements anatomical imaging.

name: Radionuclide ventriculography
definition: A gated nuclear study that tracks labelled blood within the ventricles to measure ventricular volumes, ejection fraction, and wall motion.
clinical_significance: It quantifies global and regional ventricular function and can help monitor changes when precise ejection-fraction measurement is needed.

name: Regurgitation
definition: Backward flow of blood through a valve that fails to close completely during the relevant phase of the cardiac cycle.
clinical_significance: Valve regurgitation causes volume overload and chamber remodelling; acute severe regurgitation can cause pulmonary oedema or low cardiac output.

name: Renal
definition: Relating to the kidneys, the organs that regulate fluid, electrolyte, acid-base balance, and blood-pressure physiology.
clinical_significance: Kidney disease strongly influences cardiovascular risk and volume status, while renal perfusion can fall during heart failure or shock.

name: Restenosis
definition: Recurrent narrowing of an artery after it has been opened by angioplasty, stenting, or another revascularisation procedure.
clinical_significance: Restenosis can reproduce angina or limb ischaemia and may require repeat imaging or revascularisation; mechanisms include neointimal growth and vessel recoil.

name: Revascularization
definition: Restoration of blood flow to an underperfused tissue by bypass surgery, angioplasty, stenting, thrombus removal, or another intervention.
clinical_significance: Revascularisation can relieve ischaemia and preserve viable myocardium or limb tissue, with choice determined by anatomy, symptoms, and clinical risk.

name: Rheumatic fever
definition: An immune-mediated inflammatory illness that can follow infection with group A Streptococcus, affecting joints, skin, brain, and the heart.
clinical_significance: Cardiac inflammation may scar valves and cause chronic rheumatic heart disease, especially mitral stenosis or regurgitation.

name: Rheumatic heart disease
definition: Chronic valvular heart disease caused by the scarring and remodelling that follow rheumatic fever.
clinical_significance: Valve stenosis or regurgitation can produce atrial enlargement, atrial fibrillation, pulmonary hypertension, heart failure, and thromboembolism.

name: Right ventricular assist device (RVAD)
definition: A mechanical pump that supports blood flow from the right ventricle or right atrium into the pulmonary artery.
clinical_significance: RVAD support can treat severe right-ventricular failure temporarily or alongside left-sided support, but bleeding, thrombosis, infection, and pulmonary complications may occur.

name: Risk factor
definition: A characteristic, exposure, or condition associated with an increased probability of developing a disease or adverse event.
clinical_significance: Recognising modifiable and non-modifiable cardiovascular risk factors supports risk estimation and explains why atherosclerosis or complications are more likely.

name: Rubella
definition: A contagious viral infection, also called German measles, caused by rubella virus.
clinical_significance: Maternal infection can cause congenital rubella syndrome, which may include congenital heart defects such as patent ductus arteriosus or pulmonary-artery stenosis.

name: Saccular aneurysm
definition: A rounded, pouch-like aneurysm projecting from only part of an arterial circumference.
clinical_significance: Its focal wall weakness may enlarge, thrombose, embolise, dissect, or rupture, with risk determined by vessel, size, and morphology.

name: Sarcoidosis
definition: A multisystem inflammatory disease characterised by non-caseating granulomas in affected organs.
clinical_significance: Cardiac sarcoidosis can cause conduction block, ventricular arrhythmia, myocardial dysfunction, heart failure, or sudden death even when lung disease is limited.

name: Saturated fat
definition: A dietary fat whose fatty-acid chains contain no carbon-carbon double bonds and are found in varying amounts in animal and plant foods.
clinical_significance: High intake can raise LDL cholesterol compared with unsaturated fat and thereby contribute to atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk.

name: Second-degree heart block
definition: Intermittent failure of atrial impulses to conduct to the ventricles, producing dropped QRS complexes; patterns include Mobitz I and Mobitz II.
clinical_significance: It can cause bradycardia, pauses, dizziness, or syncope and may progress to complete heart block, particularly in more distal conduction disease.

name: Septal defect
definition: An abnormal opening in the septum separating the atria or ventricles, allowing blood to pass between chambers.
clinical_significance: The direction and size of the shunt determine whether it causes volume overload, cyanosis, pulmonary hypertension, paradoxical embolism, or few effects.

name: Septum
definition: The muscular or membranous partition separating the right and left chambers of the heart.
clinical_significance: Septal structure is essential for separating oxygenated from deoxygenated blood; defects or hypertrophy can alter flow, conduction, and ventricular function.

name: Sheath
definition: A hollow vascular access tube that permits insertion, exchange, and withdrawal of catheters during an endovascular procedure.
clinical_significance: It maintains stable access for intervention but can cause access-site bleeding, vessel injury, thrombosis, or infection.

name: Shock
definition: A state of circulatory failure in which tissue oxygen delivery is inadequate for metabolic needs, despite compensatory responses.
clinical_significance: Cardiogenic shock results from severe pump failure and causes organ hypoperfusion, lactic acidosis, and high mortality; other forms include hypovolaemic and distributive shock.

name: Shunt
definition: An abnormal or deliberately created pathway that allows blood to flow between two vascular beds or cardiac chambers.
clinical_significance: A shunt can alter oxygenation and impose volume or pressure load; surgical shunts may palliate congenital heart disease by redirecting pulmonary blood flow.

name: Sick sinus syndrome
definition: A group of sinus-node disorders causing inappropriate bradycardia, sinus pauses, chronotropic incompetence, or alternating bradycardia and atrial tachyarrhythmia.
clinical_significance: It can cause fatigue, dizziness, syncope, and atrial fibrillation and may require rhythm monitoring or pacing when symptoms correlate with pauses.

name: Silent ischemia
definition: Objective myocardial ischaemia occurring without the person experiencing typical anginal chest pain.
clinical_significance: It may be detected by ECG, ambulatory monitoring, stress testing, or imaging and can delay recognition of coronary disease or infarction.

name: Sinus (SA) node
definition: The sinoatrial node, a specialised group of cells in the right atrium that normally initiates the heart’s electrical rhythm.
clinical_significance: Its rate sets the basic heart rhythm; dysfunction can cause sinus bradycardia, pauses, chronotropic incompetence, or alternating atrial tachyarrhythmias.

name: Sodium
definition: An essential electrolyte that is the principal extracellular cation and helps regulate fluid balance, nerve activity, and muscle function.
clinical_significance: Sodium and water balance influence blood volume and blood pressure; excess retention contributes to congestion in heart failure, while severe abnormalities can disturb rhythm and neurological function.

name: Sphygmomanometer
definition: An instrument that measures arterial blood pressure using an inflatable cuff and pressure sensor or column.
clinical_significance: Accurate measurement is fundamental to diagnosing and monitoring hypertension, hypotension, and haemodynamic change.

name: Stem cells
definition: Cells capable of self-renewal and differentiation into one or more specialised cell types.
clinical_significance: Stem-cell biology is relevant to developmental cardiology and regenerative research, but potential cardiovascular therapies depend on specific cell type and evidence.

name: STEMI
definition: A ST-segment-elevation myocardial infarction, an acute myocardial infarction associated with persistent ST elevation or an equivalent ECG pattern indicating acute transmural ischaemia in the appropriate context.
clinical_significance: STEMI commonly reflects acute coronary occlusion and carries risk of extensive myocardial damage, arrhythmia, shock, and mechanical complications.

name: Stent
definition: A mesh or tube-like prosthesis deployed inside a narrowed or weakened vessel to support its lumen and maintain blood flow.
clinical_significance: Coronary and peripheral stents improve vessel patency after angioplasty, but thrombosis, restenosis, migration, or fracture can occur.

name: Stenosis
definition: Abnormal narrowing of a tubular passage, such as an artery, vein, or heart-valve orifice.
clinical_significance: Stenosis increases resistance to flow and creates upstream pressure or downstream underperfusion; clinical effects depend on location and severity.

name: Stethoscope
definition: An acoustic instrument used to hear internal body sounds, including heart sounds, murmurs, breath sounds, and vascular bruits.
clinical_significance: Auscultation can provide clues to valve disease, heart failure, lung congestion, and turbulent arterial flow, although findings often require imaging confirmation.

name: Stokes-Adams disease
definition: Syncope or near-syncope caused by transient complete atrioventricular block or prolonged pauses, historically associated with third-degree heart block.
clinical_significance: The underlying pause can produce profound cerebral hypoperfusion, seizures, injury, or sudden death and indicates serious conduction-system disease.

name: Streptococcal infection (“strep” infection)
definition: An infection caused by bacteria of the genus Streptococcus, including throat and skin infections caused by group A Streptococcus.
clinical_significance: Untreated or recurrent group A streptococcal infection can precede rheumatic fever and chronic rheumatic valve disease; invasive infection can also cause sepsis.

name: Streptokinase
definition: A thrombolytic protein that forms a complex with plasminogen and promotes conversion to plasmin, which degrades fibrin clots.
clinical_significance: It can restore flow by dissolving thrombus in selected emergencies, but systemic bleeding and intracranial haemorrhage are important risks.

name: Sternum
definition: The flat bone forming the front of the central thoracic cage and articulating with the ribs and clavicles.
clinical_significance: The sternum is the principal landmark and access route for median sternotomy in many open cardiac operations.

name: Stress
definition: A state of physiological or psychological strain produced by internal or external demands.
clinical_significance: Acute stress activates sympathetic and hormonal responses that raise heart rate and blood pressure; chronic stress may interact with behavioural and metabolic cardiovascular risks.

name: Stroke
definition: A sudden neurological deficit caused by focal brain infarction from vascular occlusion or intracranial haemorrhage.
clinical_significance: Stroke can cause permanent disability or death; determining whether it is ischaemic or haemorrhagic is central to diagnosis and treatment selection.

name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
definition: Bleeding into the cerebrospinal-fluid space between the arachnoid membrane and pia mater, often from a ruptured intracranial aneurysm.
clinical_significance: It can cause sudden severe neurological injury, raised intracranial pressure, vasospasm, and secondary cerebral ischaemia.

name: Subclavian arteries
definition: Paired arteries arising from the brachiocephalic trunk or aortic arch that supply the upper limbs and contribute branches to the neck and brain.
clinical_significance: Subclavian stenosis can cause arm ischaemia or vertebrobasilar symptoms and can reverse flow through the vertebral artery or affect bypass graft perfusion.

name: Sudden death
definition: Unexpected death occurring within a short interval of symptom onset, commonly from an abrupt cardiac or neurological event.
clinical_significance: Sudden cardiac death most often results from ventricular arrhythmia in structural or electrical heart disease, though coronary occlusion and other causes are possible.

name: Superior vena cava
definition: The large vein that returns deoxygenated blood from the head, neck, upper limbs, and upper chest to the right atrium.
clinical_significance: Obstruction causes superior vena cava syndrome with venous congestion, facial or upper-limb swelling, and collateral vein formation.

name: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT)
definition: A tachyarrhythmia arising from atrial tissue or the atrioventricular junction, with ventricular activation above the bundle branches and usually a narrow, rapid rhythm.
clinical_significance: SVT can cause palpitations, hypotension, dyspnoea, or syncope; recurrent rapid rates may impair ventricular function.

name: Syncope
definition: A brief loss of consciousness and postural tone caused by transient global cerebral hypoperfusion, followed by spontaneous recovery.
clinical_significance: Cardiac syncope may indicate bradyarrhythmia, tachyarrhythmia, structural obstruction, or inadequate output and carries potential risk of injury or sudden death.

name: Systolic blood pressure
definition: The highest arterial pressure reached during ventricular contraction, represented by the upper number in a blood-pressure measurement.
clinical_significance: Persistent elevation reflects increased arterial load and predicts vascular events, left-ventricular hypertrophy, stroke, and heart failure.

name: Tachycardia
definition: A heart rate faster than expected for age and clinical context, usually referring to an adult resting rate above 100 beats per minute.
clinical_significance: Tachycardia may be physiological or arrhythmic; sustained rapid rates can reduce filling, lower output, cause ischaemia, or produce cardiomyopathy.

name: Tachypnea
definition: An abnormally rapid respiratory rate for age and clinical context.
clinical_significance: It may reflect pulmonary congestion, hypoxia, metabolic acidosis, pain, infection, or circulatory stress and is an important sign when assessing heart failure or shock.

name: Tamponade
definition: Cardiac tamponade is compression of the heart by accumulated fluid, blood, or gas in the pericardial space, limiting diastolic filling.
clinical_significance: Reduced filling lowers stroke volume and cardiac output and can cause obstructive shock; the severity depends on the rate and volume of accumulation.

name: Thallium-201 stress test
definition: A nuclear myocardial-perfusion study using thallium-201 uptake during stress and rest to display regional blood flow and viable myocardium.
clinical_significance: Reversible perfusion defects suggest inducible ischaemia, whereas persistent defects may represent scar or nonviable tissue.

name: Third-degree heart block
definition: Complete atrioventricular block in which no atrial impulses conduct to the ventricles, leaving the ventricles dependent on a slower escape rhythm.
clinical_significance: It can cause profound bradycardia, low output, syncope, heart failure, or cardiac arrest and generally signifies advanced conduction disease.

name: Thrombolysis
definition: The enzymatic breakdown of fibrin within a blood clot, either naturally or through a thrombolytic medicine.
clinical_significance: Restoring flow by dissolving thrombus can limit infarction in selected arterial occlusions, but bleeding is the major treatment-related hazard.

name: Thrombosis
definition: Formation of a blood clot within a blood vessel or heart chamber during life, potentially obstructing flow.
clinical_significance: Thrombosis can cause myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, limb ischaemia, DVT, or pulmonary embolism depending on its location and embolic behaviour.

name: Thrombolytic therapy
definition: Treatment with medicines that activate plasminogen or otherwise promote dissolution of fibrin-rich intravascular thrombi.
clinical_significance: It can reopen an occluded artery or vein in selected time-sensitive conditions, but eligibility is limited by the risk of major or intracranial bleeding.

name: Thrombus
definition: A blood clot formed within a blood vessel or cardiac chamber that remains attached to its site of formation.
clinical_significance: A thrombus can obstruct local flow or detach as an embolus and cause infarction in a distant organ.

name: Thyroid
definition: An endocrine gland in the front of the neck that produces thyroid hormones regulating metabolism, growth, and energy use.
clinical_significance: Thyroid excess or deficiency can alter heart rate, rhythm, vascular resistance, lipid levels, and cardiac contractility.

name: Tissue plasminogen activator (tPA)
definition: A naturally occurring or recombinant protein that converts plasminogen to plasmin and promotes fibrin clot breakdown.
clinical_significance: Recombinant tPA can restore flow in selected acute thrombotic conditions, but its use can cause serious bleeding, including intracranial haemorrhage.

name: Trans fat
definition: An unsaturated fat containing at least one trans-configured carbon-carbon double bond, produced industrially or occurring in small amounts in some animal foods.
clinical_significance: Industrial trans fat raises LDL and lowers HDL cholesterol and increases atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk.

name: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI)
definition: A procedure that delivers and deploys a replacement aortic valve through a catheter, usually without surgical removal of the native valve; also called TAVR.
clinical_significance: TAVI relieves severe aortic stenosis in selected patients and avoids open-heart surgery, while risks include vascular injury, stroke, conduction block, and paravalvular leak.

name: Transcatheter intervention
definition: A cardiovascular procedure performed by advancing instruments through a blood vessel to diagnose or treat a cardiac or vascular lesion.
clinical_significance: It permits revascularisation, valve treatment, ablation, or structural repair without open surgery, with risks related to access, embolisation, bleeding, and vessel injury.

name: Transesophageal echocardiography
definition: Ultrasound imaging of the heart from a probe positioned in the oesophagus behind the heart.
clinical_significance: It provides high-resolution views of valves, atria, aorta, thrombus, and endocarditis when transthoracic images are inadequate or during procedures.

name: Transient ischemic attack (TIA)
definition: A transient episode of neurological dysfunction caused by focal brain, spinal-cord, or retinal ischaemia without established tissue infarction.
clinical_significance: TIA is a warning of future stroke and indicates a need to identify embolic, large-artery, or small-vessel mechanisms.

name: Transplantation
definition: Transfer of an organ, tissue, or cells from a donor or another site to replace or support diseased tissue in a recipient.
clinical_significance: Heart transplantation can restore circulation in selected end-stage heart failure, but rejection, infection, graft vasculopathy, and immunosuppressant toxicity remain concerns.

name: Tricuspid valve
definition: The three-leaflet atrioventricular valve between the right atrium and right ventricle.
clinical_significance: Tricuspid stenosis obstructs right-sided filling, while regurgitation causes systemic venous congestion and may reflect right-ventricular or pulmonary disease.

name: Triglyceride
definition: A molecule consisting of glycerol esterified to three fatty acids and the principal form of stored fat and circulating dietary fat.
clinical_significance: Elevated triglycerides often accompany metabolic disease and atherogenic lipoproteins and, at very high levels, increase pancreatitis risk.

name: Ultrasound
definition: Imaging that uses high-frequency sound waves and their echoes to display tissues, organs, or moving blood.
clinical_significance: Ultrasound is fundamental to echocardiography and vascular assessment because it provides structural and haemodynamic information without ionising radiation.

name: Valve replacement
definition: Surgical or transcatheter replacement of a diseased heart valve with a mechanical or biological prosthesis.
clinical_significance: Replacement restores forward flow or limits regurgitation when native-valve disease causes obstruction, symptoms, ventricular dysfunction, or other clinically important consequences.

name: Valvuloplasty
definition: A procedure that enlarges or reshapes a narrowed heart-valve opening, usually with a balloon catheter or surgical technique.
clinical_significance: It can reduce stenotic obstruction and improve forward flow, although restenosis, valve regurgitation, embolism, or residual obstruction may occur.

name: Varicose vein
definition: A superficial vein that is persistently enlarged, elongated, and tortuous because of venous-valve incompetence or increased venous pressure.
clinical_significance: Varicose veins can cause aching, oedema, skin changes, bleeding, or superficial thrombophlebitis, but are distinct from deep-vein thrombosis.

name: Vascular
definition: Relating to blood vessels, including arteries, veins, capillaries, and lymphatic vessels when specified.
clinical_significance: The term encompasses diseases and procedures involving vessel structure, flow, inflammation, thrombosis, or vascular access.

name: Vasodilators
definition: Medicines or other agents that relax vascular smooth muscle and widen blood vessels.
clinical_significance: Vasodilation lowers vascular resistance or venous pressure and can improve selected forms of hypertension, angina, heart failure, or pulmonary vascular disease; hypotension may result.

name: Vasopressors
definition: Medicines that raise vascular tone and arterial pressure, usually through adrenergic or other vasoconstrictor receptors.
clinical_significance: They support perfusion in selected forms of shock but can increase cardiac afterload, provoke ischaemia, and reduce blood flow to peripheral tissues.

name: Vein
definition: A blood vessel that returns blood towards the heart and usually contains valves that limit reverse flow.
clinical_significance: Venous obstruction, thrombosis, or valve failure impairs return and can cause oedema, congestion, embolism, or chronic venous disease.

name: Ventricle (right and left)
definition: One of the two lower heart chambers: the right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs and the left ventricle pumps blood to the systemic circulation.
clinical_significance: Ventricular size, pressure, and contractility determine cardiac output; ventricular failure, hypertrophy, or arrhythmia can cause severe haemodynamic compromise.

name: Ventricular Assist Device (VAD)
definition: A mechanical pump that supports blood flow from one or both ventricles to the pulmonary artery or aorta.
clinical_significance: VAD support can bridge advanced heart failure to transplantation, recovery, or long-term therapy, with risks including bleeding, infection, thrombosis, stroke, and right-heart failure.

name: Ventricular fibrillation
definition: Chaotic ventricular electrical activity that produces uncoordinated contraction and no effective forward blood flow.
clinical_significance: It is a cause of cardiac arrest and requires immediate defibrillation for a meaningful chance of restoring circulation.

name: Ventricular tachycardia
definition: A rapid cardiac rhythm arising from ventricular myocardium, consisting of three or more consecutive ventricular beats.
clinical_significance: It may cause palpitations, hypotension, syncope, or cardiac arrest and often indicates myocardial scar or another structural or electrical substrate.

name: Vertigo
definition: A false sensation that the person or surroundings are spinning or moving, usually caused by vestibular or neurological dysfunction.
clinical_significance: Vertigo can mimic presyncope or complicate assessment of stroke; associated focal neurological signs may indicate a cerebrovascular cause.

name: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome
definition: A pre-excitation syndrome in which an accessory atrioventricular pathway conducts impulses around the AV node, producing a characteristic ECG pattern and susceptibility to tachyarrhythmia.
clinical_significance: Re-entry can cause episodic supraventricular tachycardia, and rapid conduction during atrial fibrillation may produce dangerous ventricular rates.

name: X-ray
definition: Imaging that uses ionising radiation to create projections or computed images of internal structures.
clinical_significance: Chest and vascular X-ray-based studies can show heart size, pulmonary congestion, device position, calcification, or contrast-filled vessels, depending on the examination.
